She accused him of physical assault, harassment, and making death threats towards her. In response, Sahu released a video alleging that Arya's claims are based on an AI-generated audio clip. Arya has alleged corruption against Sahu, claiming he is responsible for her political rise.

articles.title: 'Things got excessive after divorce': Yuzvendra Chahal opens up on alcohol addiction
articles.summary: Yuzvendra Chahal revealed his struggles with alcohol following his divorce and the importance of rehabilitation. He checked into a rehab centre for 26 days to regain control over his life. Chahal emphasized that he recognized the need to stop drinking to protect his cricket career. While he has faced personal challenges, he remains a leading wicket-taker in the IPL. His experiences have contributed to his emotional maturity and overall well-being.

articles.title: 'Can't replace capability': Starlink disruption exposes Ukraine's reliance on US tech
articles.summary: EU leaders are addressing concerns regarding Ukraine's reliance on Elon Musk's Starlink satellite for military communications. Disruptions to the Starlink service have highlighted the urgent need for European alternatives. Officials discussed how to strengthen Europe's satellite communication capabilities during a recent summit with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Investor interest in European satellite companies, such as Eutelsat and SES, has surged after the disruptions.

articles.title: Dak Prescott's $240 million Cowboys contract in 2024 included $231 million guaranteed
articles.summary: Dak Prescott signed a four-year, $240 million contract extension with the Dallas Cowboys in September 2024, including $231 million in total guaranteed money and an $80 million signing bonus. The deal made him the NFL’s highest-paid player by average annual value at $60 million per season. Dallas secured its franchise quarterback through 2028, betting on his leadership and passing ability to end the team’s long Super Bowl drought.

articles.title: NBA star Deandre Ayton pledges $100,000 to rebuild Jamaica after 2025 hurricane
articles.summary: Deandre Ayton demonstrates his dedication to community service through his active participation in the PMBL Youth Basketball Camp in Jamaica. His Ayton Family Foundation engages in vital hurricane recovery efforts and provides access to food resources. This camp annually welcomes over 1,500 children, offering free meals, supplies, and enriching experiences.

articles.title: Tennessee man turns backyard pool into 500,000-gallon water playground
articles.summary: In Covington, Tennessee, Micky Thornton transformed a childhood aspiration into reality by building a vast backyard pool. Initially a family retreat, this impressive space evolved into a gathering hub, hosting everything from birthday celebrations to weddings. Notably, it has become a venue for over 400 baptisms, deepening its community ties. Thornton's journey showcases that the pursuit of extraordinary dreams demands patience and dedication to refining one’s vision.

articles.title: UK shopper paid £1 for first-edition James Bond book; it later sold for £10,000
articles.summary: A woman bought a book at a car boot sale in Yorkshire for just £1 ten years ago. She later discovered it was a rare first edition of Casino Royale by Ian Fleming. The book retained its original dust jacket and was valued significantly. It was auctioned for £10,000, highlighting the importance of rarity and condition in collectibles. The successful bidder was a UK collector specializing in Ian Fleming editions.

articles.title: Taylor Swift gave 6,000 books to struggling library; 15 years later, it thrives
articles.summary: In 2011, Taylor Swift generously donated 6,000 books to bolster local libraries in Berks County amid looming budget cuts. This pivotal support allowed the Reading Public Library to enrich its programs and attract thousands of community members. By 2025, the library circulated over 182,000 items and continued to foster engagement through various initiatives, proving Swift’s contribution remains vital for the region's library services to this day.

articles.title: Black ink on Tagore: The fight over Bangladesh's identity
articles.summary: The recent defacement of Rabindranath Tagore's portrait in Dhaka has stirred a fresh wave of conversations about his legacy. Against the backdrop of increased political unease post the July 2024 uprising and claims against Jamaat-e-Islami, public outcry highlights the threat to cultural icons. This event has mobilized protests and reinvigorated discussions, reflecting on the vital intersection of politics, culture, and the essence of national identity in contemporary Bangladesh.

articles.title: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards in 2027; first time in over 70 years
articles.summary: Pakistan will assume the chairmanship of the IMF and World Bank Group boards in 2027, marking a significant return. This follows a long absence from the position that last occurred in 1953. The role will allow Pakistan to engage in global economic discussions and foster collaboration among member nations. Pakistan is currently utilizing financial assistance from the IMF through various programs aimed at economic stabilization.

articles.title: Japan issued a 9.9 magnitude earthquake alert, but ground didn't shake: What happened

Although the alert caused temporary disruptions in transportation, officials are now investigating the warning system to ensure public safety and prevent future confusion.

articles.title: Court tells US to process Green Card applications for up to 55,000 people by these dates

articles.title: Spotting drones before it's too late: US Army eyes wearable detection tech
articles.summary: The US Army is currently examining innovative wearable tech that provides soldiers with real-time alerts about incoming hostile drones during engagements. This compact sensor leverages unique acoustic signatures for immediate warnings, prioritizing soldier safety without burdening them with extra gear. Insights from the ongoing conflict in Ukraine underscore the necessity of advanced drone detection systems, ultimately aiming to bolster the effectiveness and protection of troops on the front lines.

articles.title: EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
articles.summary: While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits. In a rare, all parties in Punjab hail CEC, 'transparent' SIR exercise
articles.summary: Punjab’s final electoral rolls have recorded a net decline of 13.60 lakh voters from the pre-SIR electorate, but the revision has drawn rare cross-party praise. Representatives of the AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD commended Chief Electoral Officer Anindita Mitra for transparency, consultation and addressing their concerns. Their endorsement comes amid protests against the Election Commission elsewhere, offering a striking contrast as Punjab’s voter list settles at just over 2.01 crore electors.

articles.title: 'He never chased that reward': Ashwin reveals what drove Bhuvneshwar's India comeback
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's selection for the T20I series against New Zealand showcases his impressive form with RCB. Ravichandran Ashwin emphasized that Bhuvneshwar concentrated on honing his skills instead of aiming for a comeback on the national team. Ashwin is optimistic about India's prospects in the upcoming 2027 ODI World Cup, attributing this to solid bowling assets and seasoned hitters. He pointed out South Africa's strength, citing their understanding of local conditions.

articles.title: Flydubai attack: UAE detains 2 Maldivian pilots over links with accused co-pilot - report
articles.summary: Authorities have detained two Maldivian pilots in connection with the flydubai stabbing incident that occurred recently. The stabbing incident involved Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami attacking Indian pilot Smit Machchhar with an axe. Despite serious injuries, Machchhar managed to unlock the cockpit and stabilize the aircraft with crew assistance. Investigators are exploring al-Hammami's alleged extremist links and how he was hired by flydubai.

articles.title: US issues power grid emergency in 13 states: Reason and what it means for residents
articles.summary: In a decisive move to ensure grid stability during a peak demand period, US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has empowered PJM Interconnection to manage local power generation units from October 13 to October 16. With temperatures hitting unseasonably high levels, demand has surged to approximately 111,500 megawatts on October 13. While residents are not required to take action, voluntary conservation measures may be recommended.

articles.title: Germany's Nuremberg Airport suspends flights after suspected aviation emergency
articles.summary: Nuremberg Airport experienced a temporary flight suspension after receiving reports of a suspected aviation emergency. Police confirmed the aircraft from Corfu landed safely amid the investigation. Eurofighter jets accompanied the plane, ensuring safety during the landing process. Additionally, there were earlier reports of a possible drone sighting near the airport, which authorities could not verify. This follows heightened concerns in Germany regarding drone incidents near critical infrastructure.

articles.title: ‘Not invited to party’: Bareilly teen stabbed repeatedly by neighbour, dies
articles.summary: In Gokulpur village, a 17-year-old boy named Arjun was fatally stabbed by his neighbor after a dispute. The disagreement arose when Vishal, who was allegedly drunk, was upset over not being invited to a birthday party. He confronted Arjun, who attempted to calm him down but was violently attacked instead. Angry villagers subsequently assaulted Vishal and locked him in a house until police arrived.

articles.title: Sensex ends 1,100 points higher, investors richer by Rs 4.12 lakh crore: Why markets are up today
articles.summary: Stock market rally today: BSE Sensex ended the day at 73,033.78, up 1,109 points or 1.54%. Nifty50 closed at 22,721.95, up 359 points or 1.60%.The rally added more than Rs 4.12 lakh crore to the combined market capitalisation of listed companies, taking the total to Rs 470 lakh crore.

articles.title: No AC, yet naturally cool: Begum's 149-year-old palace now lies in ruins
articles.summary: Benazeer Palace, built in 1877, was once a symbol of architectural marvel and royal heritage. The palace features a unique cooling system using natural airflow and has many beautiful halls that remain intact. Despite undergoing restoration, it has not been effectively utilized and faces deterioration today. There was a proposal to transform it into a heritage hotel, though progress remains uncertain.

articles.title: Ben Affleck-backed initiative delivers 100m litres of clean water in Congo
articles.summary: In 2010, Ben Affleck established the Eastern Congo Initiative to foster development in the Democratic Republic of Congo. By 2024, this organization has provided over 100 million litres of clean water across various regions and facilitated access to essential health services for more than 400,000 individuals. The initiative’s social enterprise, Asili, is crucial in delivering sustainable services, showcasing the power of community-driven solutions in tackling humanitarian issues.

articles.title: Long Island’s 127-room Oheka Castle heads to auction with $63.5m debt
articles.summary: Oheka Castle, the largest residence on Long Island, will be auctioned on 27 October. The mansion, designed in 1919, is burdened with over $63.5 million in debt. Since its purchase in 1984, the current owner invested about $50 million in restoration efforts. The property also has development potential with approved plans for 95 luxury condominiums. Prospective buyers must provide a $750,000 deposit to participate in the auction.

articles.title: Sergey Brin is biggest donor against California wealth tax; could owe $13 billion
articles.summary: Sergey Brin has donated $102 million to oppose California's proposed wealth tax during the upcoming election. Brin's contributions aim to combat a measure that could impose a 5% tax on billionaires. Other wealthy individuals, including Eric Schmidt and Peter Thiel, have joined Brin in opposing this tax. Governor Gavin Newsom also expresses concern about potential impacts on the state's economy and public services.

articles.title: Hailee Steinfeld’s NSFW cheer goes viral after Josh Allen’s clutch Bills play

Her lively reaction came at a pivotal moment right before a touchdown, showing a stark contrast to her usually discreet support at games. This unexpected burst of enthusiasm highlighted her genuine love for the sport and showcased a more personal side of her fandom in front of the cameras.

articles.title: Aaron Donald’s fight with O’Cyrus Torrence sparks fan backlash over NFL comeback

With the reason behind the confrontation still unclear, attention remains on his conduct and performance.

articles.title: Fruit farmer faced tax notice over large cash deposits in bank; what ITAT said
articles.summary: A farmer from Bengaluru faced a tax notice regarding unexplained cash deposits into his bank account. He was able to present evidence supporting his agricultural income claims, which led to a favorable ruling. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal evaluated the documents submitted, including land records and APMC sale bills. The tribunal found that the lack of detailed records did not invalidate the farmer's claims.

Simon Cowell donated £25,000 to help rescue over 200 dogs from meat farm
articles.summary: In 2018, Simon Cowell donated £25,000 to Humane Society International to help close a dog meat farm in South Korea. The charity rescued nearly 200 dogs and puppies, including animals suffering from untreated injuries and poor living conditions. The dogs were sent to shelters in the US, UK, Canada and the Netherlands for care and possible adoption.

articles.title: Grand Canyon trout removal helps native fish populations rise over 400%
articles.summary: Historically, Bright Angel Creek was a sanctuary for various native fish species, including the endangered humpback chub. However, the rise of non-native brown trout has threatened this ecosystem. In an effort to restore balance, the Bright Angel Creek Trout Reduction Project was initiated, successfully eliminating invasive trout and leading to a remarkable 400% increase in native fish populations.

articles.title: Michael Dell-backed firm spent $375m upgrading Boca Raton resort; 40% condos sold
articles.summary: An impressive $875 million investment is set to transform The Boca Raton resort into a luxurious haven of residential condominiums. With around 40% of these high-end residences already reserved, pricing starts at $8.95 million and can exceed $20 million. This revitalization forms part of the resort's centennial celebrations scheduled for 2026, with construction commencing the same year and concluding by 2029.

articles.title: Most Americans think Trump is profiting from presidency unethically or illegally
articles.summary: A recent poll revealed that a majority of Americans think Donald Trump is profiting illegally or unethically from his presidency. The survey indicated that around 60% of respondents believe Trump is prioritising personal financial interests over helping regular citizens. Financial disclosures suggested Trump has received significant investments in cryptocurrency ventures since returning to office. Concerns about Trump's financial conduct varied widely among political affiliations, with many Democrats alleging wrongdoing.

articles.title: Maharashtra man beats wife to death, walks into police station to confess
articles.summary: In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, a man named Mukesh Kumbhakarna allegedly killed his wife, Rohini, during an argument. The couple had recently returned to Kannad town for the festive season. Following the incident, Kumbhakarna went to the local police station and confessed to the crime. Authorities have registered a murder case against him and an investigation is currently ongoing.

articles.title: Who is Neha Bora? Meet the JNUSU leader and AISA president
articles.summary: Neha Bora, the national president of the All India Students’ Association, has attracted attention through student protests and her recent detention in Delhi. Born in Khatima, Uttarakhand, she studied sociology at Hindu College, pursued postgraduate studies at Dr B. R. Ambedkar University and joined Jawaharlal Nehru University for PhD research in theatre and performance studies. Her journey from street theatre to activism includes a 23-day hunger strike and campaigns against examination centralisation.

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana retains No. 1 spot in ODI rankings; Ellyse Perry returns to top 10
articles.summary: Smriti Mandhana remains the highest-ranked batter in the ICC women’s ODI rankings with 790 rating points. Harmanpreet Kaur maintains her place in the top ten at ninth position. The T20I batting rankings feature three Indian players, with Shafali Verma leading in fourth place. Indian bowlers dominate the T20I bowling rankings, with Shree Charani in the top spot. India maintains a strong presence in both ODI and T20I team rankings.

articles.title: Gym trainer arrested for rape; accused of making obscene videos of 80 women
articles.summary: A 22-year-old gym trainer, Arif Shaikh, has been taken into custody following grave accusations from a 23-year-old woman. She alleges that Arif raped her multiple times under the guise of a promise of marriage and coerced her into changing her religion. The complainant further claims that he deceived several women and recorded intimate videos without their consent.

articles.title: 3 times cheaper than Patriot? US firm Anduril unveils Steelfin interceptor
articles.summary: Anduril Industries has unveiled the Steelfin family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles, specifically crafted to meet evolving air defense requirements. These advanced interceptors efficiently neutralize threats such as drones and cruise missiles while maintaining cost-effectiveness. Their modular design allows for tailored configurations across diverse missions, streamlining production. Full-rate manufacturing is anticipated to commence by late 2028 or early 2029 following rigorous testing.

articles.title: Qatar Airways, travel portal ordered to pay Rs 3L after denying patient a ticket refund
articles.summary: A passenger was diagnosed with a brain tumour and had to cancel an international trip. He requested a refund from Qatar Airways and EaseMyTrip, providing medical documents. Despite his request, he was denied a refund and offered a reduced amount. The Hyderabad consumer commission found both companies responsible and ordered them to provide a full refund. Additionally, they must pay compensation for mental distress and litigation costs.

articles.title: Ohio brothers bought flooded quarry for $330,000; village later drops seizure bid
articles.summary: Two Ohio brothers bought a flooded quarry for $330,000 in 2005 and spent 15 years improving it before a dispute with the Village of Luckey disrupted their planned sale. After nearly five years of litigation, the village abandoned its attempt to acquire the property through eminent domain but now faces a $206,000 legal bill, with the settlement still under dispute.Is this conversation helpful so far?

SBI Research suggested abolishing LTCG tax on equity investments to stabilize foreign capital flows. Additionally, she emphasized investment opportunities in infrastructure, semiconductors, and renewable energy as India’s economic fundamentals remain strong. The Reserve Bank of India is focused on reducing rupee volatility rather than fixing its value.

articles.title: MDR on UPI transactions over Rs 2,000 deferred; to come into effect post Diwali
articles.summary: The government has announced a delay in implementing the Merchant Discount Rate for Unified Payments Interface transactions, pushing back the launch initially scheduled for October 15 to after Diwali. This postponement aims to avoid potential payment disruptions amid the festive shopping surge, allowing payment companies additional preparation time for the upcoming changes. This initiative was expected to generate new revenue streams for these companies.

articles.title: Meet Harrison Nott, 16, whose bedroom towel business now makes £750,000 a year
articles.summary: Harrison Nott, a 16-year-old entrepreneur from Essex, England, started CoolTowel in his bedroom in 2023. After winning a global pitching competition and attracting investor Rio Ferdinand, his cooling towel business generated over £750,000 in revenue this year. Despite sales success, stock shortages, copycats and operating costs remain challenges as he pursues profitability full-time.

Nasa's Perseverance rover breaks 15-year Mars driving record
articles.summary: Nasa’s Perseverance rover has surpassed Opportunity by covering 45.22 km on Mars in five and a half years. The rover broke this record on October 11, during its 2,006th Martian day of the mission. Perseverance's autonomous navigation has been vital, accounting for over 90 percent of its driving distance. Additionally, it has discovered signs of ancient microbial activity and explored geological features within Jezero Crater.

articles.title: Asian Para Games 2026 India squad: Full list of 166 athletes across 10 sports
articles.summary: India’s Sports Ministry has greenlit a team of 275 individuals for the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. This contingent includes 166 talented athletes across ten disciplines, featuring standout players like gold medallist Sheetal Devi and world champion Pramod Bhagat. Para-athletics leads the representation, closely followed by para-badminton and para-swimming, highlighting emerging athletes. The games will take place from October 18 to 24, 2026.

articles.title: Caught on cam: Punjab anti-drug activist shot dead after confronting chemist over 'drug sales'
articles.summary: Parwinder Singh Jhota was involved in a sting operation targeting a medical store in Mansa. He confronted the store owner about selling prohibited substances and had a heated exchange before being shot. Despite his attempts to escape, Jhota fell and was pronounced dead at the hospital. The police have identified the shooter, Ashwani Kumar, who fled after the incident.

articles.summary: Nüshu, an ancient script developed by women in Jiangyong County, China, served as a vital means of communication in a society dominated by men. Through this remarkable writing system, women conveyed their innermost thoughts and shared personal experiences. Although it nearly faded into obscurity, recent resurgence among young women and scholars has sparked new efforts for preservation, including national heritage recognition and artistic exploration to keep its legacy vibrant.

articles.title: Ohio protects 5,165 acres across 58 family farms from future development

Through the Local Agricultural Easement Purchase Program, farmers can keep cultivating their land while ensuring its preservation. Presently, more than 111,000 acres across 62 counties are safeguarded from development. With federal funding poised to enhance these efforts, local sponsors can apply for the 2027 program for further conservation.

It clarified that it had not approved changes to the declaration regarding electoral rolls. The court's remarks arose during a hearing on the functioning of the Election Commission of India. Concerns were raised over the legality of the changes introduced in Form 6. The Supreme Court will further examine this issue in October.

Local volunteer groups and community members support her conservation efforts and engage in cultural activities.

Many schools have reported that examinations cannot proceed effectively due to insufficient staff availability. articles.title: Australia removed rabbits; petrel colony grew to over 800 breeding pairs
articles.summary: After the successful elimination of rabbits from Cabbage Tree Island, conservationists observed a remarkable increase in the Gould’s petrel population. This pivotal action mitigated serious threats to their habitat and reproductive success, leading to over 800 breeding pairs by 2000, with annual offspring exceeding 400. To further bolster the species, a second breeding colony was initiated on Boondelbah Island, emphasizing the need for ongoing protective measures.

articles.title: Bronze Age child burials reveal gender-linked funeral customs 4,000 years ago
articles.summary: The study of burial practices in Bronze Age Serbia indicates that children’s funerary treatment varied by biological sex, with research focused on two Maros culture cemeteries. Boys and girls were interred in contrasting ways, highlighting established gender roles. Interestingly, some burials challenged these customs, inviting reflection on societal standards. This work sheds light on the nuances of how ancient communities perceived and enacted gender distinctions in funerary rituals.

articles.title: Bill Gates-backed malaria nets helped fight disease, but are harming African waters

This alarming practice not only jeopardizes fish populations but also poses a serious threat to fragile aquatic ecosystems. Food-insecure families find this adaptation as a quick fix, but the harmful chemicals in the nets could also endanger marine life. A comprehensive strategy is essential to harmonize health measures with ecological integrity.
